items.stem: Which practice best supports least privilege in Google Cloud IAM?

options.text: Grant predefined or custom roles scoped to the needed resource
options.rationale: Correct: narrowly scoped roles follow least privilege.

options.text: Grant the basic Owner role to all engineers
options.rationale: Owner is overly broad and violates least privilege.

options.text: Share one service account key with the team
options.rationale: Shared keys are insecure and over-permissioned.
Disabling auditing reduces governance, not privilege scope.

items.explanation: Correct: scoped predefined/custom roles support least privilege.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO reduce the risk from service account credentials? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use workload identity federation instead of exported keys
options.rationale: Correct: federation avoids long-lived downloadable keys.

options.text: Attach a service account to the resource rather than exporting a key
options.rationale: Correct: attachment avoids key handling entirely.

options.text: Email the key to all developers
Commit the key JSON to the git repo

items.explanation: Correct: federation and attached service accounts avoid risky keys.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: How do IAM policies behave across the resource hierarchy?

options.text: Child resources inherit allow policies from ancestors (org, folder, project)
options.rationale: Correct: allow policies are inherited down the hierarchy.

options.text: Policies apply only to the exact resource and never inherit
options.rationale: Inheritance is a core IAM behavior.

options.text: A project policy overrides the organization's billing

options.rationale: Inheritance applies to all principals, not just service accounts.

items.explanation: Correct: allow policies inherit down the hierarchy.
